root_text: @mrmickme2 It’s critically important to have multimodal rapid tests available to distinguish rsv/flu/sars/adeno/hmpv. These are available outside the U.S.  Also need to rapidly subtype, preferably POC, if it’s flu.

nodes.text: @ariccio @mrmickme2 It’s not clear if infected cases have been vaccinated, or if sick because of vaccine mismatch, waning, or virus drift. Not clear that a mid season boost would be helpful. If more data from these cases were made available, more options to reduce impact could be considered.

nodes.author: ariccio
nodes.text:
That's one of the things where I have none of the proper technical knowledge to really understand.
It seems to me like there's data that supports a small or modest benefit:
https://t.co/PBIAT3hNjV

In the scheme of acute hospitalization or death, not that big. But given the evolving knowledge of longer term impacts of flu infections, even a 10-20% improvement in protection could save a TON of kids from new health problems

nodes.author: ariccio
nodes.text: @RickABright @mrmickme2 (*the part about not knowing if it would be helpful - other than that no questions as to whether we need more data on these cases in particular!)
